title: AlphaProof Code: Machine-Code Formal Verification of Signal Protocol
whyItMatters: First protocol-level mathematical security proofs for the unmodified compiled machine code of a globally deployed cryptographic protocol—completed in four weeks.
summary: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent AI system that produced machine-checked Lean proofs establishing core security guarantees—including post-compromise security and post-quantum key exchange properties—directly on the compiled AArch64 Linux binary of Signal's unmodified libsignal (v0.105.4) and SPQR (v1.6.0) Rust crates. A five-person team completed the verification in four weeks.
technicalHighlights: Operates directly on compiled AArch64 machine code rather than idealized abstract protocol models, eliminating compiler and implementation-gap vulnerabilities.
Proves post-compromise security and post-quantum key exchange guarantees in Lean.
Demonstrates an order-of-magnitude reduction in the human-effort cost of formal verification for production software.
caveats: Proof guarantees hold relative to the formal security specification and trusted computing base (§5.3 of the technical paper); hardware side-channels and out-of-spec runtime assumptions remain outside the verified boundary.

scoreRationale.foundational: Breaks the decades-old scalability barrier separating formal methods from real-world compiled cryptographic software.
scoreRationale.ripple: Establishes a practical blueprint for mathematically verifying critical infrastructure: OS kernels, TLS stacks, browsers, and avionics.
scoreRationale.verification: Machine-checked Lean proofs with public specifications and verification artifacts released for independent inspection.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed what historically required tens of person-years of formal-methods labor into four weeks with five researchers.
